restructure.title: HL.7 is a process layer and should be removed
restructure.detail: The reviewed audit AUDIT-03 records the verdict of HL.7 as process. Its three targets are: exporting explicit residue and reciprocity maps to Brauer obstructions, arithmetic duality and motivic cohomology with commutative comparison diagrams; developing complete small examples of a two-dimensional field and a regular arithmetic surface; and maintaining separate formal statements for currently unproved extensions. The audit says of the second that it repeats the acceptance examples of HL.0 and HL.5, and of the third that it is bookkeeping. The job's own instructions say that a process layer is not mathematics, gets no nodes, and that its removal is to be proposed here. Proposal: remove HL.7. Its first target is a link job between HL.4 and HL.6 on one side and the consumer roadmaps on the other, and should be filed as such once those maps exist; its second is already planned in HL.0 and HL.5; its third is what the coverage records and the gaps of this packet do.

restructure.title: HL.1 is almost entirely K2SymbolsBrauer's, and its stage text should say so
restructure.detail: AUDIT-03 records three duplicates for HL.1, all against K2SymbolsBrauer: T.2 already defines Milnor K-theory in all degrees as the tensor algebra modulo the homogeneous Steinberg ideal, which is HL.1's first target verbatim; T.3 plans the tame residues with signs, the higher Milnor residues, the transfers and the norm and residue formula with ramification and residue degree, which are HL.1's boundary maps and projection formulas; and T.4 constructs the Milnor transfers through the Bass-Tate sequence. The packets for T.1 to T.7 exist and this packet imports from them by node identifier. What is left for HL.1 is the iterated residue attached to a residue tower with its sign rule, the compatibility of that residue with the norm through the ramification matrix, and the topological Milnor K-groups. Proposal: rewrite HL.1's stage text to say that the Milnor K-theory, the one-step residues and the transfers are imported from K2SymbolsBrauer:T.2 to T.4, and that HL.1 owns the tower-specific constructions. As written, the text reads as though the whole of Milnor K-theory were to be built here.

restructure.title: The source tags AE-HLFVOLUME and AE-HLCFT are not defined anywhere in the repository
restructure.detail: Six stage texts of this roadmap name AE-HLFVOLUME and two name AE-HLCFT as their source route, and one of the latter gives the page range 165 to 195. Neither tag appears in any reference register, catalogue or guide in the repository; a worker has to guess what they denote. Both in fact resolve to the same freely available volume, Invitation to higher local fields, Geometry and Topology Monographs 3 (2000): it is the volume of the higher local fields conference, and Kato's Existence theorem for higher local class field theory occupies exactly its printed pages 165 to 195. Proposal: record the resolution of both tags, with the URL and the SHA-256 this packet gives, wherever the campaign source tags are kept, so that the next worker on any of the eight layers does not have to rediscover it.

restructure.title: HL.6 should be divided, because its two halves have different sources and different states
restructure.detail: HL.6 asks for four things: the assembled reciprocity map and its comparison with the abelian etale fundamental group; the tame and wild, proper and open variants as separate theorems; Kato complexes with the vanishing of the square of the boundary; and the cohomological Hasse principles. The third is a construction that follows from HL.5's residue maps and the sign convention of HL.1, and can be carried out from the sources this packet has. The other three need a primary source that nobody in this programme has yet obtained, and the stage text itself says that the local volume does not prove them. As one layer HL.6 can never be closed and a reader cannot see which part is reachable. Proposal: divide HL.6 into HL.6:complexes, carrying Kato complexes and the boundary-square-zero statement, and HL.6:reciprocity, carrying the global comparison, its four variants and the Hasse principles, with the primary-source selection recorded as that sub-layer's first obligation.
